case_title: SISTER MINA LALITA BARUWA v. STATE OF ORISSA AND OTHERS
neutral_facts: The accused, a group of individuals, were alleged to have brutally assaulted and gang-raped the victim, a Catholic nun, during a communal violence incident in Kandhamal District. The victim was sheltered by a priest at a residence and later dragged out by a mob, where she was subjected to sexual assault. The victim filed a complaint and was medically examined. The prosecution conducted a test identification parade, but there was a discrepancy in the evidence provided by a judicial officer who conducted the parade. The victim approached the public prosecutor to rectify the error, but the application was rejected by the trial court. The victim then appealed to the High Court, which also dismissed the application, citing limitations on the private party's role under Section 301 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The Supreme Court found serious irregularities in the handling of the case and directed the trial court to recall the judicial officer as a witness and allow cross-examination to address the discrepancy in the evidence.
